channel.title: OT/ICS Threat Intel - All Critical Infrastructure
channel.description: Curated OT/ICS advisories, incidents and threat intelligence. Editorial by Mike Holcomb in partnership with UtilSec.

item.title: [Critical] Citrix patches two actively exploited NetScaler zero-days after a week of unpatched attacks
item.description: Citrix released fixes on 27 September for two remote-code-execution flaws in NetScaler ADC and Gateway that it confirmed were being actively exploited on unmitigated appliances. CVE-2026-88771, an improper input-validation flaw, lets an unauthenticated attacker run commands on a default configuration; CVE-2026-88772, a memory-overflow flaw exploitable when DTLS is enabled, the default for VPN virtual servers, can cause remote code execution or a crash. Both score CVSS v4.0 9.5. The disclosure caps roughly a week of uncertainty: watchTowr first reported active exploitation on 26 September, before Citrix had published any advisory, CVE, or fix, and some administrators were advised to shut appliances down as a precaution. NetScaler Gateway is a common remote-access front door into OT DMZs and vendor-support paths, so the exposure window mattered directly to industrial operators, not just enterprise IT. - Citrix security bulletin; reported by watchTowr, Cyber Kendra and SecurityWeek - Exploitation reported 26 Sep 2026; Citrix fixes published 27 Sep 2026; added to CISA KEV 27 Sep 2026

item.title: [Critical] Colorado confirms foreign hackers tampered with two small water systems’ pumps and alarms
item.category: Incident — confirmed foreign intrusion into two small, privately owned drinking-water systems; equipment settings, pumping cycles and alarms altered; no known impact to treatment or public safety; actors unidentified; no development since disclosure
item.description: Gov. Jared Polis’s office confirmed on 18 September that foreign cyber actors breached two small, privately owned Colorado water systems in late August, changing equipment settings, disabling remote access and alarms, and altering pumping cycles. Officials say the disruption was brief, with no known impact on water treatment, water quality or public safety. The office says it cannot confirm which foreign actors were involved; federal officials are separately tracking an Iranian-backed effort against US water systems, but no link to these intrusions has been confirmed. It remains the only confirmed OT-tampering incident in this edition, with no new development reported as of 27 September. - Colorado Governor’s office statement, reported by Axios Denver and Industrial Cyber - Intrusions late Aug 2026; confirmed 18 Sep 2026 — no new development as of 27 Sep

item.title: [High] Tanker campaign: a third vessel’s cyberattack claim stays unverified as a Texas regulator urges operators to harden
item.category: Incident — cyber intrusions on two tankers boarded by the Coast Guard and FBI in August confirmed; a third vessel’s cyberattack claim unverified; a Texas commissioner’s statement cites the boardings; no confirmed operational disruption ashore; attribution unresolved
item.description: The Coast Guard and FBI boarded two foreign-flagged energy tankers bound for US ports in late August, including the VL Prosperity, bound for Galveston. A third vessel, the LNG carrier Vivit Africa LNG, lost access to some internal control systems in early September while bound for Italy with a Louisiana cargo, and diverted toward Spain; Bloomberg first reported it on 18 September. The crew’s claim that attackers seized pressure and safety-valve systems is unverified, and Italy’s Coast Guard recorded a cargo-monitoring malfunction of undetermined cause. On 24 September Texas Railroad Commissioner Wayne Christian cited the August boardings in a statement urging the state’s oil and gas operators to “invest, test, monitor and strengthen our defenses now.” No official development has been reported since. - US Coast Guard and FBI via Cybernews; Bloomberg and Splash247 on Vivit Africa LNG; Railroad Commission of Texas release (Commissioner Wayne Christian) - Boardings late Aug 2026; third vessel reported 18 Sep 2026; Texas statement 24 Sep 2026 — no official development since

item.title: [High] A cyber incident stopped container handling at Tanjung Pelepas — the restart began with manual gate-ins
item.category: Incident — confirmed cyber incident; container terminal operations and terminal operating systems suspended at one of the world’s largest transhipment hubs; phased manual restart; a ransomware leak-site listing is unconfirmed by the operator
item.description: A cyber incident detected late on 9 September forced Malaysia’s Port of Tanjung Pelepas to suspend container terminal operations and its terminal operating systems as a precaution. A phased restart from 10 September initially used manual processing for export container gate-ins, and the port says operations have resumed with system recovery advancing. PTP, a joint venture between MMC Group and APM Terminals, is among the largest transhipment hubs anywhere. For OT defenders it is a clean example of the pattern that actually causes industrial downtime: nothing reported suggests crane or equipment controls were touched — losing the system that decides where each container goes was enough to stop the boxes moving. - Port of Tanjung Pelepas spokesperson and Maersk statements, reported by WorldCargo News and The Loadstar - Incident 9 Sep 2026; phased restart from 10 Sep; resumption statement 15 Sep 2026 — no new development as of 27 Sep

item.title: [High] Chained flaws in an IO-Link master give an unauthenticated attacker root — and a say over sensor and actuator data
item.category: Research — Nozomi Networks Labs technical write-up of CERT@VDE VDE-2026-014: 19 CVEs in a Pepperl+Fuchs IO-Link master, led by CVE-2026-27546 (CVSS v3.1 9.8); chained for unauthenticated root; fixed firmware available; no known exploitation
item.description: Nozomi Networks Labs published a technical write-up on 24 September of flaws in the Pepperl+Fuchs IO-Link master ICE2-8IOL-K45P-RJ45 (EtherNet/IP firmware 1.7.3), coordinated through CERT@VDE as VDE-2026-014. Nozomi details 19 CVEs, led by CVE-2026-27546, an authentication bypass rated CVSS v3.1 9.8, alongside OS command-injection flaws rated 8.8 and 7.2 and a path traversal rated 7.5. Chained, they give an unauthenticated attacker root on the device, with the ability to manipulate the sensor and actuator data passing through it. CERT@VDE’s 16 September advisories list 20 CVEs, two at CVSS v3.1 9.8, across Pepperl+Fuchs, Phoenix Contact and Carlo Gavazzi IO-Link masters. These devices bridge field sensors to the controller, a layer many OT monitoring programs don’t cover. - Nozomi Networks Labs; CERT@VDE advisories VDE-2026-014, -027 and -028 - Advisories 16 Sep 2026; Nozomi technical write-up 24 Sep 2026

item.title: [Medium] Stolen remote-access logins for US water utilities are already circulating, SpyCloud finds
item.category: Research — SpyCloud infostealer-exposure analysis of 10,000 US water and wastewater utilities and their technology vendors; OT or remote-access credentials exposed at 258 organizations; exposure, not confirmed intrusion; no CVE
item.description: SpyCloud analyzed stolen-identity data linked to 10,000 US water and wastewater utilities and their technology vendors and found active infostealer exposure at 1,787 of them; 258 had exposed credentials for OT or remote-access systems. In one case, a single infected device at a major US advanced-metering technology provider held saved logins for about 167 utility metering portals. Tools named include TeamViewer, LogMeIn, GoToMyPC and SonicWall and Fortinet management portals. SpyCloud stresses that it measures identity exposure, not confirmed intrusion, and does not tie the findings to any actor or campaign; nothing links them to the Colorado intrusions — but stolen remote-access credentials are one of the most direct routes to the pumps and alarms small utilities depend on. - SpyCloud research; reported by SecurityWeek (25 Sep) - Published 20 Sep 2026

item.title: [High] A third MikroTik router flaw joins CISA’s exploited list as attacks at the OT remote-access edge continue
item.category: Advisory — CVE-2026-67279 (SSH workflow bypass) joins CVE-2026-86060 and CVE-2026-67277 in CISA KEV for MikroTik RouterOS; confirmed active exploitation via the “MikroTrick” SSH chain since ~2 Sep; fixed firmware available
item.description: CISA added a third MikroTik RouterOS flaw, CVE-2026-67279, to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 25 September, joining CVE-2026-86060 and CVE-2026-67277 from 10 September. CERT Polska has tracked in-the-wild exploitation since roughly 2 September of a two-flaw SSH chain it calls “MikroTrick,” which hands an unauthenticated attacker full administrative control when chained with CVE-2026-86060. Shadowserver separately counted more than 122,500 internet-reachable MikroTik devices in early September — an exposure figure, not a confirmed-unpatched count. These routers commonly front remote-access and cellular-telemetry links into field sites and small, unattended facilities that rarely get timely firmware updates. - CISA KEV catalog (25 Sep release) and CERT Polska; reported by The Hacker News - Disclosed and patched early Sep 2026 (CERT Polska, 5 Sep); CVE-2026-86060/67277 added to CISA KEV 10 Sep; CVE-2026-67279 added 25 Sep 2026 (due 28 Sep)

item.title: [Critical] Check Point’s federal KEV deadline has passed for two exploited flaws — the VPN gateway that fronts the plant and the server that writes its rules
item.category: Advisory — CVE-2026-85102 (Security Gateway and Spark with VPN, certificate validation) and CVE-2026-93616 (management servers and SmartEvent, path traversal), Check Point; both exploited in the wild; added to CISA KEV 22 Sep 2026, federal deadline 25 Sep 2026, now passed
item.description: Check Point has confirmed exploitation of two flaws. CVE-2026-85102, improper certificate validation on Security Gateways and Spark firewalls using site-to-site or remote-access VPN, enables unauthenticated remote code execution; patches shipped 9 September and an exploitation wave from VPN and proxy anonymization infrastructure began on 12 September. CVE-2026-93616, a pre-authentication path traversal in Security Management Server, Multi-Domain Security Management, Log Servers and SmartEvent, lets an unauthenticated attacker upload and execute scripts and was exploited as a zero-day in a handful of pinpointed attacks on 23 July. CISA added both to KEV on 22 September with a 25 September deadline, which has now passed. Check Point gateways commonly sit at the IT/OT boundary and at small unmanned sites. - Check Point sk1000117 and CISA KEV (22 Sep 2026); reported by BleepingComputer and Help Net Security - Gateway fix 9 Sep 2026; exploitation from 12 Sep 2026 (gateway) and 23 Jul 2026 (management); KEV addition 22 Sep 2026; federal deadline 25 Sep 2026

item.title: [High] About a thousand small Zyxel switches were compromised through a flaw patched in June
item.category: Advisory — CVE-2026-7273, Zyxel GS1900 managed switches; stack-based buffer overflow in the CGI web interface; 996 switches reported compromised; added to CISA KEV 21 Sep 2026, federal deadline 24 Sep 2026 passed; fix available since June
item.description: GreyNoise reported on 21 September that 996 Zyxel GS1900 managed switches in 48 countries had been compromised through CVE-2026-7273 since about mid-August. The flaw is a stack-based buffer overflow in the switches’ CGI web interface that lets an unauthenticated attacker on the local network potentially execute operating-system commands; firmware 2.90(XXXX.1)C0 and earlier is affected, and Zyxel released a fix in June. CISA added it to KEV on 21 September with a 24 September deadline, now passed. GreyNoise describes the actor as Chinese-speaking and links it to the one behind earlier WordPress and Gitea exploitation. Small managed switches like the GS1900 are common in plant and utility networks, where firmware updates often lag. - CISA KEV catalog; GreyNoise research reported by Help Net Security and The Hacker News - Fix June 2026; KEV addition 21 Sep 2026; GreyNoise report 21 Sep 2026

item.title: [Critical] A broken authentication check in the Modicon M580 leaves safety controllers exposed for as long as change control takes
item.category: Advisory — CVE-2026-3869 (CVSS v4.0 9.2; v3.1 9.8), Schneider Electric Modicon M580 and M580 Safety controllers; incorrect authentication-algorithm implementation; fixed firmware available, no known exploitation
item.description: Schneider Electric’s notice SEVD-2026-251-04, published 8 September, discloses CVE-2026-3869: an incorrect implementation of an authentication algorithm (CWE-303) in Modicon M580 and M580 Safety programmable controllers that lets an attacker bypass an authentication check. It scores CVSS v4.0 9.2 and v3.1 9.8. Affected are M580 below application level 4.00 and M580 Safety below application level 4.20. No public exploitation has been reported, but the M580 is a widely deployed controller family, and validation and change-control requirements routinely keep plants on older firmware for weeks or quarters after a fix ships — a gap defenders need to cover with compensating controls. - Schneider Electric security notification SEVD-2026-251-04 - Published 8 Sep 2026

item.title: [High] A single malformed packet can crash the time-series database embedded in many OT historians and IIoT pipelines
item.category: Advisory — CVE-2026-42542 (CVSS 7.5), TDengine open-source time-series database; pre-authentication integer-underflow denial of service; fix available, no known exploitation
item.description: Ridge Security disclosed CVE-2026-42542 on 23 September: a pre-authentication integer-underflow flaw in TDengine, the open-source time-series database widely embedded in industrial telemetry, historian and IIoT monitoring pipelines. A malformed packet with an undersized length field sent to TDengine’s RPC handler on TCP 6030 triggers an arithmetic wraparound that reaches a memory-copy call, crashing the database process with no authentication or user interaction required. Affected versions run 3.4.0.0 through 3.4.1.5; 3.4.1.6 fixes it. Ridge Security says it has no telemetry indicating in-the-wild exploitation and is not aware of public exploit code. TDengine instances bundled inside historian or IIoT platforms are easy to miss in an asset inventory built around PLCs and HMIs, and no credentials are needed to knock one over. - Ridge Security research; CVE-2026-42542 public record - Published 23 Sep 2026

item.title: [Info] FBI and CISA: your ICS integrator’s access to your plant is your risk too, not just theirs
item.category: Guidance — FBI and CISA fact sheet “Considerations for Critical Infrastructure Operators Working With Third-Party ICS Integrators,” motivated by a 2025 compromise of a US industrial automation/SCADA integrator; no CVE, no new confirmed operator intrusion
item.description: The FBI and CISA published a joint fact sheet, “Considerations for Critical Infrastructure Operators Working With Third-Party ICS Integrators,” prompted by a 2025 compromise of a US industrial automation solutions company that provided system integration, engineering consulting and SCADA programming. Between March and April 2025, the agencies say, foreign intruders searched the company’s systems for terms including “customers” and “SCADA” and staged nine archives of roughly 800 files of customer SCADA information, ICS device details and schematics for exfiltration; the downstream customers named are power utilities and transportation entities. The fact sheet recommends least-privilege access for integrators, on-demand and auditable remote access, a full inventory of supplied hardware and software, security requirements in contracts, and the ability to operate manually if the integrator is compromised. - FBI and CISA joint fact sheet; reported by Industrial Cyber and SecurityWeek - Fact sheet dated 23 Sep 2026; released 24 Sep 2026

item.title: [Info] NIST’s core OT security guide gets a major rewrite — and the comment window is open until 30 November
item.category: Guidance — NIST releases initial public draft of SP 800-82 Revision 4, “Guide to Operational Technology (OT) Security”; expanded sector scope, restructured around CSF 2.0; comment period through 30 Nov 2026; no CVE
item.description: NIST released the initial public draft of SP 800-82 Revision 4, “Guide to Operational Technology (OT) Security,” on 21 September. The draft expands coverage beyond classic ICS to include building automation, water and wastewater, food and agriculture, freight rail, maritime vessels and industrial IoT and cloud convergence; restructures the document around NIST Cybersecurity Framework 2.0, with the risk section refocused on the Govern function; and expands guidance on asset management, network monitoring and zero-trust architecture for OT. Public comments are open through 30 November 2026. It landed the same week as the FBI and CISA fact sheet on third-party ICS integrator risk (above). - NIST Computer Security Resource Center; reported by SecurityWeek - Draft published 21 Sep 2026; comments due 30 Nov 2026
